example2_zh: 学校附近的诊所，让生病的孩子更容易看病然后回家。
collocations: near to｜靠近 ; nearby｜在附近
tip_zh: near 可作介词、形容词或副词。nearly 是“几乎”，不是“附近”。

meanings_zh: v. 流动 | n. 流动；流量
definition_en: to move steadily, like water | a steady movement
example1_en: The stream flows under the bridge.
example2_en: Traffic should flow past a school gate, not stop across the crossing.
example2_zh: 车流应当从校门口经过，而不是停在斑马线上。
collocations: flow into｜流入 ; the flow of｜……的流动
tip_zh: flow 作名词是流动或流量。

definition_en: a mother or father
example1_en: A parent must sign the form.
example1_zh: 必须有家长在表上签字。
example2_en: Parents who work late need a meeting time that is not in the middle of the afternoon.
example2_zh: 下班晚的家长需要一个不是下午正中的见面时间。
collocations: parent of｜……的家长
tip_zh: parent 可数。parents 常指双亲。

meanings_zh: n. 电梯 | v. 举起
definition_en: a machine that carries people between floors; British | to raise
example1_en: The lift is out of order.
example2_en: A lift that stops is a problem for the student who cannot use the stairs.
example2_zh: 停运的电梯对不能走楼梯的学生是问题。
collocations: take the lift｜乘电梯
tip_zh: 英式 lift 是电梯，美式常用 elevator。作动词是举起。

definition_en: known by many people
example1_en: The town is famous for its lake.
example2_en: A famous name on a poster does not prove that the advice is right for teenagers.
example2_zh: 海报上的著名名字，并不能证明那条建议适合青少年。
collocations: be famous for｜因……闻名 ; be famous as｜作为……闻名
tip_zh: 因某事闻名用 famous for；作为某种身份闻名用 famous as。

definition_en: an arrangement to meet at a set time
example1_en: The appointment is at four.
example2_en: An appointment at the clinic should not depend on a bus that has already stopped.
example2_zh: 诊所的预约不应当依赖已经停运的公交。
collocations: make an appointment｜预约 ; an appointment with｜与……的约定
tip_zh: appointment 也可指任命。

definition_en: the anniversary of the day someone was born
example1_en: Her birthday is in March.
example2_en: A birthday in term time is easier to share when the class does not expect an expensive gift.
example2_zh: 学期中的生日，如果班级不期待昂贵的礼物，就更容易一起过。
collocations: birthday party｜生日聚会 ; happy birthday｜生日快乐
tip_zh: birthday 是每年的生日。birth 是出生，本批另有词条。

definition_en: a yellow fat made from milk
example1_en: There is butter on the bread.
example2_en: Butter left in the sun is not safe for lunch.
example2_zh: 放在太阳下的黄油用来做午饭不安全。
collocations: bread and butter｜黄油面包
tip_zh: butter 通常不可数。

definition_en: a place of higher or further education
example1_en: He hopes to study art at college.
example2_en: A college far from cheap housing leaves students working nights just to pay the rent.
example2_zh: 远离廉价住房的大学，会让学生为了付房租而上夜班。
collocations: go to college｜上大学 ; college student｜大学生
tip_zh: 在美式英语里 college 常泛指大学。

meanings_zh: v. 关闭 | adj. 近的；亲密的 | adv. 接近地
definition_en: to shut | near, or intimate | near
example1_en: Please close the door quietly.
example2_en: Shops that close early leave night-shift workers with nowhere nearby to buy food.
example2_zh: 早关门的商店，让夜班工人附近没有地方买食物。
collocations: close down｜关闭 ; close to｜接近
tip_zh: close 作形容词读 /kləʊs/，表示“近的”；作动词读 /kləʊz/。

definition_en: done by or true for everyone
example1_en: The need for sleep is universal.
example1_zh: 对睡眠的需要是普遍的。
example2_en: A universal rule still fails if the form has no space for a wheelchair.
example2_zh: 如果表格没有轮椅的位置，一条普遍规则仍然会失败。
collocations: universal education｜普及教育
tip_zh: universe 已在本库。universal 是形容词。

definition_en: to stay until something happens
example1_en: Please wait for me at the gate.
example2_en: Children who wait for a bus in the dark need a light and a shelter, not only a timetable.
example2_zh: 在黑暗中等公交的孩子需要灯和候车亭，而不只是时刻表。
collocations: wait for｜等待 ; wait to do｜等着做 ; can't wait｜迫不及待
tip_zh: wait 是不及物动词，必须加 for 再接等待的对象。

definition_en: to understand, or to make something real
example1_en: I did not realize the gate was locked.
example1_zh: 我没有意识到门已经锁了。
example2_en: A town can realize a library plan only after it finds both a room and a librarian.
example2_zh: 一座城镇只有在找到房间和馆员之后，才能实现建图书馆的计划。
collocations: realize a dream｜实现梦想
tip_zh: realize 有两个常用义：明白，以及实现。英式也可拼成 realise。本库用考纲里的 realize。

definition_en: below, or less than
example1_en: The cat is sleeping under the desk.
example2_en: Children under six need shorter lessons and more time to move than a standard timetable allows.
example2_zh: 六岁以下的孩子需要比标准课表更短的课和更多活动时间。
collocations: under control｜处于控制中 ; under the age of｜未满……岁
tip_zh: under 可表示在下方，也可表示少于某个年龄或数量。

definition_en: a unit of weight, or British money
example1_en: The bag weighs one pound.
example2_en: A price in pounds should still show the number, not only the sign.
example2_zh: 用英镑标价仍然应当写出数字，而不只是符号。
collocations: a pound of｜一磅
tip_zh: pound 可数。表里这一行的音标是 potential，本库不用。

definition_en: a list of things to discuss
example1_en: The agenda is on the board.
example2_en: An agenda that hides the late bus is not the whole meeting.
example2_zh: 藏起晚班车的议程不是会议的全部。
collocations: on the agenda｜在议程上
tip_zh: agenda 可数。

definition_en: the people who live in a place
example1_en: The population of the town is growing.
example1_zh: 这个城镇的人口在增长。
example2_en: A rising population needs schools and clinics, not only more flats.
example2_zh: 增长的人口需要学校和诊所，而不只是更多公寓。
collocations: population of｜……的人口
tip_zh: population 作整体时谓语常用单数。

definition_en: belonging to one person
example1_en: Please do not read my personal notes.
example1_zh: 请不要看我的私人笔记。
example2_en: Personal data from a school app should stay with the school, not be sold.
example2_zh: 学校应用里的个人数据应该留在学校，不该被卖掉。
collocations: personal information｜个人信息
tip_zh: personal 强调属于个人；personnel 是“全体人员”，不要拼混。

definition_en: able to happen or be done
example1_en: Is it possible to finish today?
example2_en: It is possible to cut traffic if buses are frequent enough that people leave their cars at home.
example2_zh: 如果公交足够频繁、人们把车留在家里，减少车流是可能的。
collocations: as...as possible｜尽可能 ; if possible｜如果可能
tip_zh: It is possible for sb to do。possible 的主语通常是事物或 it，不是人。

definition_en: a coin worth one hundredth of a dollar
example1_en: The pencil costs fifty cents.
example2_en: A few cents on each ticket become a large sum when a whole city rides the bus.
example2_zh: 每张票上的几分钱，在全城都乘公交时会变成一大笔。
collocations: per cent｜百分之……
tip_zh: 100 cents 等于 1 dollar。百分数的 per cent 是另一个搭配。

definition_en: to take something away
example1_en: Please remove your bag from the stair.
example2_en: Schools should remove a broken step before they remove the sign that warns about it.
example2_zh: 学校应当先修掉破损的台阶，再撤掉警告的牌子。
collocations: remove sth from｜把某物从……移走
tip_zh: remove 比 take off 正式。脱衣服也可以用 remove。

definition_en: something you aim at, or a point scored
example1_en: Our goal is to finish the poster today.
example1_zh: 我们的目标是今天完成海报。
example2_en: A goal of cleaner air needs buses and trees, not only a sentence in a report.
example2_zh: 更干净空气的目标需要公交和树，而不只是报告里的一句话。
collocations: score a goal｜进球 ; achieve a goal｜实现目标
tip_zh: goal 既可指球类进球，也可指目标。

definition_en: deserving respect or attention
example1_en: The plan is worthy of a careful reading.
example2_en: A worthy goal still needs a written time.
example2_zh: 值得追求的目标仍然需要一个写下来的时间。
collocations: worthy of｜值得
tip_zh: worth 已在本库。worthy of something。表里这一行的音标是 worthwhile，本库不用。

definition_en: to speak words
example1_en: What did the coach say after the match?
example2_en: Experts say that planting trees without caring for them later wastes both money and land.
example2_zh: 专家说，种了树却不后续养护，会同时浪费金钱和土地。
collocations: say hello｜问好 ; that is to say｜也就是说
tip_zh: say 强调说的内容；tell 后面常接人：tell sb sth。

definition_en: the main subject
example1_en: The theme of the poster is water.
example2_en: A theme day works when every class can join, not only the ones with costumes.
example2_zh: 主题日要让每个班都能参加，而不只是有服装的班，才算成功。
collocations: the theme of｜……的主题
tip_zh: theme 可数。theme park 是主题公园。

definition_en: to mention, or to look at for information
example1_en: Please refer to the map on page two.
example2_en: Reports that refer to a river should also name the villages along it.
example2_zh: 提到一条河的报道，也应当写出沿岸的村子。
collocations: refer to｜提到；查阅
tip_zh: reference 已在本库。refer to 后接内容。

meanings_zh: n. 过去 | prep. 经过；晚于 | adj. 过去的
definition_en: the time before now | later than, or from one side to the other | gone by in time
example1_en: The photo shows the school in the past.
example1_zh: 照片展示了过去的学校。
example2_en: A city that forgets its past may knock down the only building that tells that story.
example2_zh: 忘记过去的城市，可能会拆掉唯一讲述那段故事的建筑。
collocations: in the past｜在过去 ; past and present｜过去和现在
tip_zh: past 作介词是“经过”：walk past the gate。half past six 是六点半。

definition_en: the part of a plant under the ground, or a cause
example1_en: The root of the tree broke the path.
example2_en: The root of the late bus is the timetable, not the driver.
example2_zh: 晚班车的根源是时刻表，不是司机。
collocations: the root of｜……的根源 ; take root｜生根
tip_zh: root 作动词是生根。

definition_en: to move something away from you
example1_en: Please push the chairs back after the talk.
example1_zh: 讲座结束后请把椅子推回去。
example2_en: Do not push onto a full bus; the next one is safer for everyone.
example2_zh: 不要往满员的公交上挤，下一辆对每个人都更安全。
collocations: push forward｜推进
tip_zh: push 作名词是“推；推力”。

definition_en: very quick
example1_en: The rapid rise in the fare was a shock.
example1_zh: 票价迅速上涨令人震惊。
example2_en: Rapid help after a flood is a dry room the same day.
example2_zh: 洪水后的迅速帮助，是当天的一间干房间。
collocations: rapid growth｜迅速增长
tip_zh: rapid 比 fast 更正式。

definition_en: a building where plays are performed
example1_en: The class visits the theatre on Thursday.
example2_en: A theatre that starts after the last bus has already chosen who can come.
example2_zh: 在末班车之后才开演的剧院，其实已经选定了谁能来。
collocations: go to the theatre｜去看戏
tip_zh: theatre 是英式拼写。美式是 theater。本库用考纲里的 theatre。

definition_en: lasting for only a short time
example1_en: The closure is temporary.
example2_en: A temporary classroom still needs heat and a toilet.
example2_zh: 临时教室仍然需要暖气和厕所。
collocations: temporary job｜临时工作
tip_zh: permanent 已在本库，是反义。

definition_en: a large amount, or a piece of land
example1_en: A lot of students take the early bus.
example2_en: A parking lot on a former playground shows what a school gives up when space becomes expensive.
example2_zh: 原来的操场变成停车场，说明当空间变贵时，学校放弃了什么。
collocations: a lot of｜许多 ; lots of｜许多 ; a lot｜很，非常
tip_zh: a lot of 既可接可数也可接不可数；too much 只接不可数。

meanings_zh: n. 罪犯 | adj. 刑事的；犯罪的
definition_en: a person who has committed a crime | related to crime
example1_en: The novel is about a criminal who returns the money.
example1_zh: 小说写一个把钱还回去的罪犯。
example2_en: Calling a teenager a criminal for a first small mistake can close doors that a warning would leave open.
example2_zh: 因为第一次小错就把青少年叫做罪犯，会关上警告本来留着的门。
collocations: criminal law｜刑法
tip_zh: 名词犯罪是 crime，已在本库。criminal 也可作形容词“刑事的”。

meanings_zh: v. 吸引 | v. 吸引靠近
definition_en: to draw interest | Pull something closer through a physical force
example1_en: Bright colors attract many insects.
example1_zh: 鲜艳的颜色吸引许多昆虫。
example2_en: Cities that invest in reliable public transport are more likely to attract businesses and skilled workers.
example2_zh: 投资建设可靠公共交通的城市更有可能吸引企业和技术人才。
collocations: attract attention｜吸引注意 ; attract tourists｜吸引游客 ; attract investment｜吸引投资 ; attract customers｜吸引顾客
tip_zh: attract是及物动词，直接接人或事物作宾语。

definition_en: the father of your parent
example1_en: Her grandfather will meet the bus.
example2_en: A form should accept grandfather or another adult name.
example2_zh: 表格应当接受祖父或其他成年人的名字。
collocations: grandfather and grandmother｜祖父母
tip_zh: father 已在本库。表里没有这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。

meanings_zh: adj. 亲爱的；昂贵的 | int. 哎呀
definition_en: loved, or costing a lot | used to show surprise
example1_en: Dear classmates, welcome to the new term.
example1_zh: 亲爱的同学们，欢迎进入新学期。
example2_en: A dear ticket can keep a family away from a museum their taxes already help to fund.
example2_zh: 昂贵的门票会把家庭挡在他们的税款已经资助的博物馆外面。
collocations: dear sir or madam｜敬启者
tip_zh: 书信开头用 Dear。英式口语里 dear 也可表示贵。作感叹词表示惊讶。

definition_en: feeling regret or sympathy
example1_en: I am sorry for being late.
example2_en: Saying sorry does not repair a leaked pipe, but refusing to say it makes neighbours angrier.
example2_zh: 说对不起修不好漏水的管子，但拒绝说会让邻居更生气。
collocations: be sorry for｜为……抱歉 ; feel sorry for｜同情
tip_zh: sorry 后接 to do 或 that 从句都可以。

meanings_zh: v. 打扰；烦恼 | v. 费心；花工夫 | n. 麻烦；烦扰
definition_en: to annoy or trouble | to make the effort to do something | trouble or effort that causes inconvenience
example1_en: Sorry to bother you so late.
example2_en: Constant notifications can bother students during lessons and reduce their ability to concentrate on complex tasks.
example2_zh: 持续不断的通知会在课堂上干扰学生，降低他们专注于复杂任务的能力。
collocations: bother someone with something｜拿某事打扰某人 ; bother to do something｜费心做某事 ; cannot be bothered｜懒得费事 ; a lot of bother｜很多麻烦
tip_zh: bother to do常用于否定或疑问，表示费心做。

definition_en: to work, to run a business, or to do surgery
example1_en: The machine does not operate without power.
example1_zh: 没有电这台机器不运转。
example2_en: Doctors operate in a hospital, not in a classroom story that skips the risks.
example2_zh: 医生在医院做手术，而不是在一个略去风险的课堂故事里。
collocations: operate on sb｜给某人动手术 ; operate a business｜经营
tip_zh: operation 已在本库。operate on 后接人或部位。本条不写手术步骤。

definition_en: a fight, or a long effort
example1_en: The history class discussed the battle.
example1_zh: 历史课讨论了那场战斗。
example2_en: The battle against a flood is won with drains and warnings, not only with courage.
example2_zh: 对抗洪水的斗争靠排水和警报取胜，而不只靠勇气。
collocations: battle against｜与……斗争 ; battle for｜为……而战
tip_zh: battle 作动词是“作战、奋斗”。

definition_en: the organ of hearing
example1_en: She whispered in his ear.
example2_en: Pain in the ear is a reason to see the clinic, not to shout.
example2_zh: 耳朵疼是去医务室的理由，不是大声喊。
collocations: by ear｜凭听觉
tip_zh: ear 可数。have an ear for 表示对声音敏感。

definition_en: in good health, or good for the body
example1_en: A healthy breakfast helps you listen in class.
example1_zh: 健康的早餐有助于你在课堂上听讲。
example2_en: A healthy canteen menu fails if the cheaper choice is always the fried one.
example2_zh: 如果更便宜的选择总是油炸的，健康的食堂菜单就会失败。
collocations: healthy food｜健康食品 ; stay healthy｜保持健康
tip_zh: healthy 形容人和有益健康的事物。health 是名词。

definition_en: very pleasant or attractive
example1_en: We had a lovely afternoon by the lake.
example1_zh: 我们在湖边度过了一个美好的下午。
example2_en: A lovely poster does not feed anyone if the canteen has already closed.
example2_zh: 如果食堂已经关门，一张好看的海报并不能让人吃上饭。
collocations: a lovely day｜美好的一天
tip_zh: lovely 多用于口语。正式写作可用 pleasant 或 beautiful。

definition_en: a way out
example1_en: The exit is at the back of the hall.
example2_en: An exit that is locked is not an exit.
example2_zh: 锁上的出口就不是出口。
collocations: fire exit｜消防出口 ; an exit from｜从……的出口
tip_zh: exit 作动词是出去。名词入口 entrance 是本批的另一词。

meanings_zh: n. 赛跑；种族 | v. 赛跑
definition_en: a competition of speed, or a group of people | to compete in a race
example1_en: She won the race by two seconds.
example1_zh: 她以两秒的优势赢了赛跑。
example2_en: A race to build the cheapest housing can ignore the drains a street will need later.
example2_zh: 竞相建造最便宜住房的竞赛，可能忽略一条街日后需要的排水。
collocations: a race against time｜争分夺秒
tip_zh: race 作动词是“赛跑”。表示种族时要慎重，避免把人简化成类别。

definition_en: a heavy sticky earth used for pots
example1_en: The pot is made of clay.
example2_en: Clay on the art-room floor becomes mud when the tap drips.
example2_zh: 水龙头滴水时，美术室地上的黏土会变成泥。
collocations: a piece of clay｜一块黏土
tip_zh: clay 通常不可数。

meanings_zh: v. 笑；大笑 | n. 笑声
definition_en: to make the sound of being amused | the sound of laughing
example1_en: We laugh at the kind joke, not at a name.
example1_zh: 我们笑善意的玩笑，不笑别人的名字。
example2_en: A class that can laugh together still needs a rule against laughing at a mistake.
example2_zh: 能一起笑的班级，仍然需要一条不许嘲笑错误的规定。
collocations: laugh at｜嘲笑；因……而笑
tip_zh: laugh at 既可以是因某事发笑，也可以是嘲笑。名词是 laughter。

definition_en: in spite of the fact that
example1_en: Although it was late, the library was still open.
example1_zh: 虽然晚了，图书馆还开着。
example2_en: Although a city builds more roads, traffic can grow if more people then choose to drive.
example2_zh: 尽管一座城市修建更多道路，如果更多人因此选择开车，交通仍可能增加。
collocations: although...｜虽然
tip_zh: although 引导的从句不能再加 but。可以加 yet 或 still。

definition_en: to discover something, often after looking
example1_en: I cannot find my student card.
example2_en: Scientists sometimes find that a cheap local method works better than an imported machine.
example2_zh: 科学家有时发现，便宜的本地方法比进口机器更有效。
collocations: find out｜查明 ; find it + adj.｜觉得……
tip_zh: find 的过去式和过去分词是 found，不是 finded。

definition_en: to give something for money
example1_en: The shop sells notebooks and pens.
example1_zh: 这家店卖笔记本和钢笔。
example2_en: Towns that sell public land beside schools may later wish they had kept a playground.
example2_zh: 卖掉学校旁边公共土地的城镇，日后可能希望当时留下了操场。
collocations: sell out｜卖完 ; for sale｜待售
tip_zh: sell 的过去式和过去分词是 sold。

definition_en: to move on foot
example1_en: We walk to school when the weather is fine.
example1_zh: 天气好时我们步行上学。
example2_en: People walk more when the pavement is wide and the crossing has a light.
example2_zh: 当人行道宽、过街处有灯时，人们会更多地步行。
collocations: walk to｜步行去 ; go for a walk｜去散步
tip_zh: walk 可作动词或名词：a ten-minute walk。

definition_en: a door or the act of going in
example1_en: The entrance is on the left.
example2_en: An entrance without a step lets a wheelchair in.
example2_zh: 没有台阶的入口能让轮椅进去。
collocations: the entrance to｜……的入口 ; entrance fee｜入场费
tip_zh: 动词 enter 已在本库。entrance 是名词。

meanings_zh: v. 跑；经营；运转 | n. 跑；一段时期
definition_en: to move quickly, manage, or operate | an act of running, or a period
example1_en: I run around the playground every morning.
example2_en: Volunteers who run a community library need a budget, not only good intentions.
example2_zh: 经营社区图书馆的志愿者需要预算，而不只是好意。
collocations: run out of｜用完 ; run after｜追赶 ; in the long run｜从长远看
tip_zh: run 的过去式是 ran，过去分词是 run。

meanings_zh: n. 谋杀 | v. 谋杀
definition_en: the crime of killing a person on purpose | to kill a person on purpose and unlawfully
example1_en: The novel opens with a murder in a small town.
example1_zh: 小说开头是小镇上的一桩谋杀。
example2_en: News about a murder should name the facts a court has, and not invite readers to invent the rest.
example2_zh: 关于谋杀的新闻应当写法院已有的事实，而不是邀请读者编造其余部分。
collocations: commit murder｜谋杀
tip_zh: murder 是故意杀人罪。事故致死不用这个词。

definition_en: an area of a town or country
example1_en: Our school is in the old district.
example2_en: A poor district can have excellent students and still lack a clinic within walking distance.
example2_zh: 一个较穷的区可以有优秀的学生，却仍然没有步行能到的诊所。
collocations: business district｜商业区 ; school district｜学区
tip_zh: district 是可数名词。

meanings_zh: v. 不同；相异 | v. 意见不合
definition_en: to be unlike | To have a different opinion from another person.
example1_en: Opinions may differ among friends.
example1_zh: 朋友之间意见可能不同。
example2_en: Educational priorities differ between countries because economic conditions and cultural expectations shape national policies.
example2_zh: 各国的教育重点有所不同，因为经济条件和文化期待会影响国家政策。
collocations: differ from｜与……不同 ; differ in size｜大小不同 ; differ widely｜差异很大 ; differ with someone｜与某人意见不同
tip_zh: from引出比较对象，in引出差异方面。

definition_en: the result of an action
example1_en: The outcome was a later bus.
example2_en: The outcome of a meeting should be written down.
example2_zh: 会议的结果应当写下来。
collocations: the outcome of｜……的结果
tip_zh: outcome 可数。

meanings_zh: n. 光；灯 | adj. 轻的；明亮的；浅色的 | v. 点燃
definition_en: brightness, or a lamp | not heavy, or bright, or pale | to start something burning
example1_en: Please turn off the light when you leave.
example2_en: Street light makes the walk home safer, but too much light can also hide the night sky.
example2_zh: 路灯让回家的路更安全，但过多的光也会遮住夜空。
collocations: traffic light｜红绿灯 ; light up｜照亮
tip_zh: light 作形容词是“轻的”或“浅色的”，比较级 lighter。作动词“点燃”的过去式可以是 lit。

meanings_zh: adj. 一般的；总体的 | adj. 大致的；非具体的 | n. 将军
definition_en: not detailed; overall | describing main points rather than particular details | an officer with a very high rank in the army
example1_en: In general, people prefer weekends.
example1_zh: 一般来说，人们更喜欢周末。
example2_en: Although the general standard of education has improved, significant differences remain between urban and rural schools.
example2_zh: 尽管教育总体水平已有提高，城乡学校之间仍存在显著差异。
collocations: in general｜一般来说 ; general public｜公众 ; general knowledge｜常识 ; general overview｜总体概述
tip_zh: in general意为“一般来说”，常用于概括。

meanings_zh: v. 责备 | n. 责任；责备
definition_en: to say someone is responsible for a fault | Responsibility for something bad that has happened.
example1_en: Don't blame others for your mistakes.
example1_zh: 不要把自己的错误归咎于别人。
example2_en: It is unfair to blame individuals alone for environmental problems caused partly by industrial activity.
example2_zh: 环境问题部分由工业活动造成，仅归咎于个人并不公平。
collocations: blame someone for something｜因某事责怪某人 ; blame something on someone｜把某事归咎于某人 ; take the blame｜承担责任 ; be to blame｜应负责任
tip_zh: 人作宾语用blame sb for；事作宾语用blame sth on。

definition_en: for all future time
example1_en: Nothing stays the same forever.
example2_en: A plastic bag lasts forever in a ditch, which is why the canteen stopped giving them out.
example2_zh: 塑料袋在沟里能留很久，所以食堂不再发放。
collocations: forever and ever｜永远
tip_zh: forever 是副词。for ever 分开写也可以，本库用 forever。

definition_en: to direct one's eyes, or to seem
example1_en: Look at the diagram before you answer.
example2_en: Streets that look beautiful in photos may still be unsafe if there is nowhere to cross.
example2_zh: 在照片里好看的街道，如果没有地方过马路，仍然可能不安全。
collocations: look for｜寻找 ; look after｜照顾 ; look forward to｜期待
tip_zh: look forward to 后面接名词或 doing。look 是看的动作，see 是看见。

definition_en: the second of two people or things
example1_en: Tea or coffee? I prefer the latter.
example1_zh: 茶还是咖啡？我更喜欢后者。
example2_en: Of the two routes, the latter stops nearer the clinic.
example2_zh: 两条路线中，后者停得离诊所更近。
collocations: the latter｜后者 ; the former｜前者
tip_zh: the latter 指两者中的后者。the former 是前者。不要用于三个以上。

definition_en: costing a lot of money
example1_en: The jacket is too expensive.
example2_en: An expensive textbook helps nobody if the library has no copy to borrow.
example2_zh: 如果图书馆没有可借的一本，昂贵的课本就帮不到人。
collocations: expensive to do｜做……很贵
tip_zh: expensive 的反义词可以是 cheap 或 inexpensive。

definition_en: a system of words used by a group
example1_en: English is not her first language.
example1_zh: 英语不是她的第一语言。
example2_en: A local language disappears faster when children never hear it outside the home.
example2_zh: 当孩子在家门外再也听不到一种本地语言时，它会消失得更快。
collocations: foreign language｜外语 ; body language｜肢体语言
tip_zh: language 可数。the English language 要加 the。

definition_en: a device that keeps a door shut | to fasten with a lock
example1_en: The lock on the lab is new.
example2_en: A lock that only one person can open is a risk if that person is ill.
example2_zh: 如果只有一个人能开的锁，那个人病了就是风险。
collocations: lock the door｜锁门 ; under lock and key｜妥善锁藏
tip_zh: lock 作动词是锁上。

meanings_zh: v. 毁坏 | n. 废墟；毁坏
definition_en: to damage something so badly that it is spoiled | the remains of a destroyed place, or the act of ruining
example1_en: The rain ruined the books.
example2_en: A hidden fee can ruin a plan that looked fair.
example2_zh: 隐瞒的费用能毁掉一个看起来公平的计划。
collocations: in ruins｜成为废墟
tip_zh: ruin 作名词常用复数 ruins，表示废墟。

definition_en: worried and unable to relax
example1_en: She was nervous before the speech.
example2_en: A nervous student still needs a turn, not only a smile.
example2_zh: 紧张的学生仍然需要一轮机会，而不只是一个微笑。
collocations: be nervous about｜对……紧张
tip_zh: nervous 形容人。

definition_en: doing something repeatedly to improve
example1_en: Piano practice is at four.
example2_en: Practice on a real street teaches road safety better than a worksheet.
example2_zh: 在真实的街道上练习，比一张练习纸更能教会交通安全。
collocations: in practice｜实际上 ; put into practice｜付诸实践
tip_zh: 英式里 practice 是名词，practise 是动词；美式动词也拼作 practice。

definition_en: the cover on top of a building
example1_en: The roof leaks when it rains.
example2_en: A school should fix the roof before it buys a new sign.
example2_zh: 学校应当先修屋顶，再买新牌子。
collocations: on the roof｜在屋顶上
tip_zh: 复数是 roofs。

definition_en: having a lot to do
example1_en: The office is busy on Monday morning.
example2_en: A busy road beside a school gate needs a crossing, not only a sign that says slow.
example2_zh: 校门口旁边的繁忙道路需要斑马线，而不只是一块写着慢行的牌子。
collocations: be busy doing｜忙于做 ; busy with｜忙于
tip_zh: 人忙用 busy。电话占线也说 The line is busy。

definition_en: not wide
example1_en: The path is too narrow for a bus.
example1_zh: 这条路窄得过不了公交。
example2_en: A narrow pavement at the gate pushes students into the road.
example2_zh: 门口狭窄的人行道把学生挤到路上。
collocations: a narrow escape｜死里逃生
tip_zh: narrow 作动词是变窄。

definition_en: to help
example1_en: The assistant will assist you with the form.
example2_en: Students assist in the library, and they still need a librarian.
example2_zh: 学生在图书馆帮忙，他们仍然需要一位馆员。
collocations: assist sb with｜帮助某人做
tip_zh: assistance 和 assistant 已在本库。assist 比 help 正式。

definition_en: to put words on paper or a screen
example1_en: Write your name at the top.
example2_en: Students write more clearly when they have a quiet place and enough time.
example2_zh: 当学生有安静的地方和足够的时间时，他们写得更清楚。
collocations: write down｜写下 ; write to｜给……写信
tip_zh: write 的过去式是 wrote，过去分词是 written。

definition_en: not in good health
example1_en: She is ill and will stay at home.
example2_en: Sending an ill child to a test spreads the illness and does not prove what they know.
example2_zh: 让生病的孩子去考试会传播疾病，也证明不了他们会什么。
collocations: fall ill｜生病 ; be ill with｜患……病
tip_zh: ill 作表语。定语常用 sick：a sick child。sick 已在本库。feel ill 和 feel sick 在英式里都常见。

meanings_zh: n. 公民 | n. 市民；居民
definition_en: a member of a country | A person who lives in a particular town or city.
example1_en: Every citizen has rights and duties.
example1_zh: 每个公民都有权利与义务。
example2_en: Every citizen should have access to reliable public services, regardless of income or place of residence.
example2_zh: 每位公民都应享有可靠的公共服务，不论收入多少或居住在哪里。
collocations: become a citizen｜成为公民 ; a senior citizen｜老年人 ; a responsible citizen｜负责任的公民
tip_zh: citizen强调公民身份；resident强调居住。

definition_en: a person who was legally owned and forced to work
example1_en: The history text names the person, not only the word slave.
example1_zh: 历史课文写出那个人的名字，而不只是奴隶这个词。
example2_en: A lesson about slavery should say that forcing people to work was wrong.
example2_zh: 关于奴隶制的课应当说明强迫人劳动是错的。
collocations: a slave of｜……的奴隶
tip_zh: 本条是历史词汇。说话时要尊重，不写强迫的做法。

definition_en: instructions for cooking a dish
example1_en: The recipe is on the card.
example2_en: A recipe that hides nuts should say so in the first line.
example2_zh: 藏着坚果的食谱应当在第一行写明。
collocations: a recipe for｜……的做法
tip_zh: recipe 可数。本条指普通食谱，不写其他配方。

definition_en: a hard piece of rock
example1_en: A stone marks the start of the path.
example1_zh: 一块石头标出小路的起点。
example2_en: Children throwing stones near a window turn a game into a repair bill.
example2_zh: 孩子在窗户附近扔石头，会把游戏变成一笔修理费。
collocations: a stone's throw｜很近
tip_zh: stone 可数。作为材料“石料”时常不可数。

definition_en: existing or happening all over the world
example1_en: The story became worldwide news.
example1_zh: 这个故事成了全世界的新闻。
example2_en: A worldwide problem such as plastic still starts with the bin outside one school.
example2_zh: 塑料这样的全球问题，仍然从一所学校外面的垃圾桶开始。
collocations: worldwide attention｜全世界的关注
tip_zh: worldwide 也可作副词。

definition_en: first in order, or most important
example1_en: Her little brother is still in primary school.
example2_en: The primary reason for the new bus is safety, and the shorter ride is only a bonus.
example2_zh: 新公交的主要原因是安全，路程变短只是附带的好处。
collocations: primary school｜小学 ; of primary importance｜最重要的
tip_zh: primary school 是小学。primary 也可表示“首要的”。

meanings_zh: n. 保证 | v. 保证；担保
definition_en: a firm promise | to promise that something will happen
example1_en: There is no guarantee that the late bus will run.
example2_en: A guarantee of a seat matters more than a bright poster.
example2_zh: 一个座位的保证比一张鲜亮的海报更重要。
collocations: guarantee that｜保证 ; under guarantee｜在保修期内
tip_zh: guarantee 作动词是担保。

definition_en: easy to see or understand
example1_en: The mistake was obvious on the first line.
example1_zh: 错误在第一行就很明显。
example2_en: An obvious gap in the bus timetable is still a gap if nobody writes it down.
example2_zh: 公交时刻表上明显的空档，如果没人写下来，它仍然是空档。
collocations: it is obvious that｜显然
tip_zh: obvious 已含“明显”，一般不必再加 very。

definition_en: the moment a baby is born, or a beginning
example1_en: The form asks for your date of birth.
example2_en: A town records every birth so the school knows how many desks it will need.
example2_zh: 城镇登记每一次出生，学校才知道将来需要多少课桌。
collocations: date of birth｜出生日期 ; give birth to｜生下
tip_zh: birthday 是生日，birth 是出生这件事。本批两条都有。

definition_en: relating to a central government of states
example1_en: The federal museum lent the town an old map.
example1_zh: 联邦博物馆借给这个城镇一张旧地图。
example2_en: Federal money for rural buses matters when a state budget cannot cover the long routes.
example2_zh: 当州预算覆盖不了长线路时，用于乡村公交的联邦资金就很重要。
collocations: federal government｜联邦政府
tip_zh: federal 多用于美国等联邦制国家的中央政府。

definition_en: a common animal kept at home
example1_en: The dog waited outside the classroom.
example2_en: A dog on a loose lead near a school gate can frighten children who are trying to cross.
example2_zh: 校门口松着绳子的狗，会吓到正要过马路的孩子。
collocations: hot dog｜热狗
tip_zh: dog 是可数名词。

definition_en: a talk that shows information
example1_en: The presentation names the source.
example2_en: A presentation about the bus should include the return time.
example2_zh: 关于公交的演示应当包括返回时间。
collocations: give a presentation｜做演示
tip_zh: 动词 present 已在本库。作名词礼物时重音不同。

meanings_zh: n. 限度；限制 | v. 限制
definition_en: the greatest amount allowed | to keep something below a level
example1_en: There is a limit of two bags.
example2_en: A speed limit near a school only helps if the sign can be seen in the rain.
example2_zh: 学校附近的限速只有在雨中也能看见标志时才有用。
collocations: speed limit｜限速 ; limit sth to｜把……限制在
tip_zh: limit 作动词是限制。a limit to 或 a limit on 都可以。

definition_en: an alcoholic drink made from grapes
example1_en: The recipe says the meat is cooked with wine.
example1_zh: 菜谱说这肉是用葡萄酒烹的。
example2_en: A school event should not treat wine as a prize for teenagers.
example2_zh: 学校活动不应当把葡萄酒当作给青少年的奖品。
collocations: a glass of wine｜一杯葡萄酒
tip_zh: wine 通常不可数。a wine 可指一种葡萄酒。

definition_en: money owed
example1_en: The club is in debt after the trip.
example2_en: Student debt is easier to discuss when the school shows the real cost of a year.
example2_zh: 当学校出示一年的真实费用时，学生债务就比较好讨论。
collocations: in debt｜负债 ; pay off a debt｜还清债务
tip_zh: debt 里的 b 不发音。in debt 表示欠债。

definition_en: a game in which you hit a small ball into holes
example1_en: The town has a public golf course.
example1_zh: 镇上有一个公共高尔夫球场。
example2_en: Golf on a school afternoon is a choice, not a requirement, if the bus home leaves at five.
example2_zh: 如果回家的车五点开，周下午的高尔夫是选择，不是要求。
collocations: play golf｜打高尔夫
tip_zh: golf 前通常不加冠词：play golf。

meanings_zh: v. 谈话；演讲 | n. 谈话；演讲
definition_en: to speak with someone | a conversation or a speech
example1_en: We talked about the class trip at lunch.
example1_zh: 午饭时我们谈了班级出游。
example2_en: Teachers who talk with students about sleep learn more than they do from a questionnaire alone.
example2_zh: 和学生谈睡眠的老师，比只看问卷了解得更多。
collocations: talk about｜谈论 ; talk to｜对……说 ; give a talk｜做演讲
tip_zh: talk 强调交谈；say 强调说出的内容。

definition_en: a hard block used for building
example1_en: The wall is brick.
example2_en: A loose brick on the step should be reported the same day.
example2_zh: 台阶上松动的砖应当当天报告。
collocations: a brick wall｜砖墙
tip_zh: brick 可数。

definition_en: a long seat
example1_en: The bench by the gate is wet.
example2_en: A bench in the shade helps the student who waits for the late bus.
example2_zh: 树荫下的长凳能帮助等晚班车的学生。
collocations: a bench of｜一条长凳
tip_zh: bench 也可指工作台。

definition_en: a mother
example1_en: My mom works at the hospital.
example2_en: A mom on a night shift may never see the school play her child is in.
example2_zh: 上夜班的妈妈可能永远看不到孩子参加的学校演出。
collocations: mom and dad｜父母
tip_zh: mom 是美式口语；英式常用 mum。正式写作可用 mother。

meanings_zh: n. 秘密 | adj. 秘密的
definition_en: something kept hidden | hidden
example1_en: Please keep the plan a secret until Friday.
example2_en: A secret about a leaking school roof helps nobody; the town needs to know.
example2_zh: 对漏雨校舍屋顶保密谁也帮不了；城镇需要知道。
collocations: keep a secret｜保密 ; in secret｜秘密地
tip_zh: secret 作形容词是“秘密的”。

meanings_zh: v. 上升；起身 | n. 上升；增加
definition_en: to go up, or to stand up | an increase
example1_en: Prices rise when the harvest is poor.
example2_en: Rivers rise quickly in this valley, so the school keeps boots by the back door.
example2_zh: 这条山谷里河水涨得快，所以学校在后门放着靴子。
collocations: rise by｜上升了 ; give rise to｜引起
tip_zh: rise 是不及物动词。及物的“举起、提高”用 raise。过去式 rose，过去分词 risen。

definition_en: a polite title for a man
example1_en: Yes, sir, I will bring the form tomorrow.
example1_zh: 是的，先生，我明天把表格带来。
example2_en: A letter that begins with Sir still fails if the request itself is unclear.
example2_zh: 以 Sir 开头的信，如果请求本身不清楚，仍然会失败。
collocations: Dear Sir｜敬启者
tip_zh: sir 单独称呼时不大写也可，但在书信 Dear Sir 中要大写。

definition_en: luck, or a large amount of money
example1_en: The fortune of the shop depends on the rent.
example1_zh: 这家店的命运取决于租金。
example2_en: A fortune on a poster does not pay the canteen staff.
example2_zh: 海报上的一大笔钱付不了食堂职工的工资。
collocations: make a fortune｜发财 ; good fortune｜好运
tip_zh: fortune 可指运气，也可指财富。

definition_en: a room where people do written work
example1_en: The teacher is in the office now.
example2_en: An office that stays lit all night wastes power and tells the street that nobody switched it off.
example2_zh: 整夜亮灯的办公室既费电，也向街道表明没人去关灯。
collocations: post office｜邮局 ; office building｜办公楼
tip_zh: in the office 表示在办公室里。

definition_en: the act of getting something
example1_en: The acquisition of a habit takes weeks.
example2_en: The acquisition of a new bus should be written down before the poster.
example2_zh: 新公交的获得应当在海报之前写下来。
collocations: the acquisition of｜获得……
tip_zh: acquisition 可数也可不可数。

definition_en: a person you know and like
example1_en: My friend lent me her notes.
example2_en: A friend who checks a rumour before sharing it protects the whole class from a false story.
example2_zh: 先核对谣言再转发的朋友，能保护全班不受假消息影响。
collocations: make friends｜交朋友 ; a friend of mine｜我的一个朋友
tip_zh: make friends with sb 表示与某人交朋友。

meanings_zh: n. 陷阱；困境 | v. 使陷入困境
definition_en: a device that catches, or a difficult situation | to put someone in a difficult situation
example1_en: The question was a trap: two answers looked right.
example1_zh: 这道题是个陷阱：两个答案看起来都对。
example2_en: A loose board on the stairs is a trap for a tired student.
example2_zh: 楼梯上松动的木板对疲惫的学生是个隐患。
collocations: a trap for｜对……的陷阱
tip_zh: trap 作动词是使陷入困境。本条不写捕捉或伤害的做法。

meanings_zh: n. 风 | v. 缠绕；蜿蜒
definition_en: moving air | to turn or twist something around
example1_en: The wind closed the classroom door.
example2_en: A strong wind along a river path can make a bike ride to school unsafe.
example2_zh: 河边路上的大风，会让骑车上学变得不安全。
collocations: strong wind｜大风
tip_zh: 作“风”时读 /wɪnd/。作“缠绕”时读 /waɪnd/，过去式是 wound。

definition_en: certain, or reliable
example1_en: Are you sure this is your bag?
example2_en: Leaders should not be sure a policy works until they have asked the people who live with it.
example2_zh: 领导者在询问真正生活在政策之下的人之前，不应确信政策有效。
collocations: make sure｜确保 ; be sure to｜一定要 ; for sure｜确实
tip_zh: be sure to do 提醒某人一定要做；make sure 后面常接 that 从句。

meanings_zh: v. 滑动 | n. 幻灯片；滑梯
definition_en: to move smoothly over a surface | a picture in a talk, or a structure to slide down
example1_en: The door will slide if you push it.
example2_en: Do not slide on a wet path.
example2_zh: 不要在湿路上滑行。
collocations: slide into｜滑进
tip_zh: slide 作名词可以是幻灯片或滑梯。

meanings_zh: n. 最大量；最大限度 | adj. 最大的
definition_en: the greatest amount possible or allowed | the greatest possible
example1_en: The maximum is two bags.
example2_en: A maximum class size means little if the room cannot hold that number.
example2_zh: 如果房间坐不下那个数，最大班额就没有意义。
collocations: a maximum of｜最多 ; maximum speed｜最高速度
tip_zh: minimum 已在本库。maximum 也可作形容词。

definition_en: to think something is probably true
example1_en: I suppose the bus is late.
example2_en: Suppose the bridge closes: the notice should already name the other path.
example2_zh: 假定桥关闭了：通知应当已经写明另一条路。
collocations: be supposed to｜应该 ; suppose that｜猜想
tip_zh: be supposed to do 表示按规定或一般认为应该。suppose 引导的祈使句表示假设。

definition_en: a person or team that wins a competition
example1_en: She is the school champion in the long jump.
example2_en: A champion who never names the team teaches the wrong lesson.
example2_zh: 从不提起队伍的冠军，教给学生的是错误的一课。
collocations: world champion｜世界冠军
tip_zh: champion 可数。动词 champion 是支持。

definition_en: a set of printed pages | to arrange to have something later
example1_en: I borrowed a book from the school library.
example1_zh: 我从学校图书馆借了一本书。
example2_en: A town that closes its bookshop loses a place where people discover titles a screen did not suggest.
example2_zh: 关掉书店的城镇，失去了一个人们发现屏幕不曾推荐的书的地方。
collocations: bookshop｜书店 ; bookmark｜书签
tip_zh: book 作动词是“预订”：book a ticket。

definition_en: the hard material from a tree
example1_en: The gate is made of wood.
example2_en: A path through the wood is pleasant in daylight and hard to follow after dark.
example2_zh: 白天穿过小树林的路很好走，天黑以后就难认了。
collocations: a piece of wood｜一块木头
tip_zh: wood 作材料不可数。woods 常指小树林。表里这一行的音标是 wonderful，本库不用。

definition_en: not public
example1_en: This is a private letter.
example2_en: Private buses may fill a gap, but they often skip the stops that make the least money.
example2_zh: 私人公交也许能补上缺口，但它们常常跳过最不赚钱的站点。
collocations: in private｜私下 ; private school｜私立学校
tip_zh: private 与 public 相对。

definition_en: the place where one lives
example1_en: I left my keys at home.
example2_en: A city that offers only expensive flats cannot call itself a home for the nurses and drivers it needs.
example2_zh: 一座只提供昂贵公寓的城市，无法成为它所需的护士和司机的家。
collocations: at home｜在家 ; go home｜回家 ; feel at home｜感觉自在
tip_zh: home 前通常不加 to：go home，不是 go to home。

definition_en: not sensible
example1_en: It was silly to leave the key in the door.
example1_zh: 把钥匙留在门上是愚蠢的。
example2_en: Calling a classmate silly is not a joke the class should keep.
example2_zh: 说同学傻，不是班级该保留的笑话。
collocations: a silly mistake｜愚蠢的错误
tip_zh: silly 可以形容行为。用在人身上会伤人。

meanings_zh: v. 修理 | n. 修理
definition_en: to fix something broken | an act of repairing
example1_en: Please repair the lock today.
example2_en: Cities should repair the crossing before they repair the paint.
example2_zh: 城市应当先修路口，再去补油漆。
collocations: under repair｜在修理中 ; repair to｜修理
tip_zh: repair 也可作名词。fix 已在本库，更口语。

meanings_zh: n. 一排；一行 | v. 划船
definition_en: a line of people or things | to move a boat with oars
example1_en: Please sit in the front row.
example2_en: A row of trees cools the path more than one poster about heat.
example2_zh: 一排树比一张关于炎热的海报更能给小路降温。
collocations: a row of｜一排 ; in a row｜连续
tip_zh: row 作“排”读 /rəʊ/。划船的动词同音。争吵的 row 读 /raʊ/，本条以“排”为主。

definition_en: money paid to a government
example1_en: The town uses tax money to repair the bridge.
example2_en: A small tax on plastic bags can change what people carry home from the market.
example2_zh: 对塑料袋征收一小笔税，可以改变人们从市场拎回家的东西。
collocations: income tax｜所得税 ; pay tax｜纳税
tip_zh: tax 作动词是“征税”。

definition_en: the smaller part of a group
example1_en: A minority of students walk; most take the bus.
example1_zh: 少数学生步行，大多数坐公交。
example2_en: A language minority still needs the notice in words they can read.
example2_zh: 使用少数语言的人，仍然需要他们能读懂的通知。
collocations: a minority of｜少数的
tip_zh: majority 已在本库。minority 可指少数，也可指少数民族。

meanings_zh: n. 日期；约会 | v. 注明日期
definition_en: a day of the month, or a planned meeting | to write the day on something
example1_en: Write the date at the top of the page.
example2_en: The date on a food label matters when a family cannot afford to throw good food away.
example2_zh: 当一个家庭扔不起还好的食物时，食品标签上的日期就很重要。
collocations: out of date｜过时 ; up to date｜最新的
tip_zh: date 作动词是“注明日期”或“约会”。

definition_en: a piece of writing or music
example1_en: The composition is due on Friday.
example2_en: A composition about the bus should include the return time.
example2_zh: 写公交的作文应当包括返回时间。
collocations: a composition of｜一篇……作文
tip_zh: composition 也可指构成。

meanings_zh: n. 遮蔽处；庇护 | v. 庇护
definition_en: a place that protects you from weather or danger | to protect someone from weather or danger
example1_en: The shelter at the stop is small.
example2_en: A shelter from the rain matters when the bus is late.
example2_zh: 公交晚点时，避雨的地方就重要。
collocations: a shelter from｜躲避……的地方
tip_zh: shelter 作动词是庇护。

definition_en: to close
example1_en: Please shut the window before you leave.
example2_en: Shops that shut at dusk leave students who finish late with a longer walk home.
example2_zh: 黄昏就关门的商店，会让下课晚的学生走更远的路回家。
collocations: shut down｜关闭 ; shut up｜住口（不礼貌）
tip_zh: shut 的过去式和过去分词仍是 shut。shut up 语气粗鲁，正式场合不要用。

definition_en: a group of people who meet for an activity
example1_en: I joined the reading club this term.
example1_zh: 这学期我加入了读书社团。
example2_en: A school club that costs money to join leaves out students who cannot pay.
example2_zh: 需要交钱才能加入的学校社团，会把付不起钱的学生排除在外。
collocations: join a club｜加入社团 ; football club｜足球俱乐部
tip_zh: club 也可指棍棒，考纲里更常见的是社团。

definition_en: a feeling, a meaning, or a way of noticing
example1_en: There is a sense of quiet in the library.
example1_zh: 图书馆里有一种安静的感觉。
example2_en: A sense of fairness grows when students see that rules apply to everyone.
example2_zh: 当学生看到规则适用于所有人时，公平感会增长。
collocations: make sense｜讲得通 ; in a sense｜在某种意义上 ; sense of humour｜幽默感
tip_zh: make sense 表示说得通，主语是事物。

definition_en: a narrow strip, or a recording strip
example1_en: The tape of the concert is in the library.
example1_zh: 音乐会的磁带在图书馆。
example2_en: Sticky tape can hold a notice, and it can also tear the paint.
example2_zh: 胶带能贴通知，也能撕掉油漆。
collocations: on tape｜录在磁带上
tip_zh: tape 作动词是用胶带粘或录音。

definition_en: the reflexive form of I
example1_en: I made the poster myself.
example2_en: I asked myself whether a shorter shower would matter if the whole building still wasted water.
example2_zh: 我问自己，如果整栋楼仍在浪费水，缩短淋浴是否还有意义。
collocations: by myself｜独自
tip_zh: myself 作宾语或同位语，不能替代 I 作主语。

definition_en: before now, or sooner than expected
example1_en: I have already handed in the form.
example2_en: By the time a warning is issued, the river may already have risen over the path to school.
example2_zh: 等到警报发出时，河水可能已经漫过上学的小路。
collocations: already finished｜已经完成
tip_zh: already 多用于肯定句；否定和疑问里表示“尚未”常用 yet。

definition_en: a room or seat for getting rid of body waste
example1_en: The toilet is at the end of the hall.
example2_en: A toilet that a wheelchair can use should be marked on the map.
example2_zh: 轮椅能用的厕所应当标在地图上。
collocations: public toilet｜公共厕所
tip_zh: toilet 可数。英式常用这个词指卫生间。

definition_en: to cover a wider area, or to open something out
example1_en: Open windows so the smell does not spread.
example1_zh: 打开窗户，免得气味扩散。
example2_en: Rumours spread faster than corrections, which is why the first notice must be accurate.
example2_zh: 谣言比更正传得快，所以第一则通知必须准确。
collocations: spread out｜散开 ; spread to｜传到
tip_zh: spread 的过去式和过去分词仍是 spread。

definition_en: a view, or the place where something happens
example1_en: The first scene of the play is a classroom.
example1_zh: 剧的第一场是一间教室。
example2_en: The scene after a flood is not only mud; it is also the question of who will repair the road.
example2_zh: 洪水之后的场面不只是泥，还有谁来修路的问题。
collocations: behind the scenes｜在幕后 ; on the scene｜在现场
tip_zh: scene 可指戏剧的一场、景色或事件现场。

definition_en: a substance used to treat illness, or the study of it
example1_en: Take the medicine after food.
example2_en: Modern medicine can treat the infection, and the clinic still has to be open.
example2_zh: 现代医学能治疗这种感染，诊所却仍然得开着门。
collocations: take medicine｜吃药 ; a medicine for｜治……的药
tip_zh: medicine 作“药”时常不可数。drug 已在本库，可指药物或毒品，写作时要分清。

definition_en: a win
example1_en: The victory belonged to the whole team.
example2_en: A victory on the field means less if the bus home is not safe.
example2_zh: 如果回家的车不安全，场上的胜利就没那么重要。
collocations: victory over｜战胜
tip_zh: victory 是名词。动词获胜用 win。

definition_en: to hit with the foot
example1_en: Do not kick the ball in the hallway.
example2_en: A rule against kicking bags under the desk saves both shins and the cleaning staff.
example2_zh: 禁止把包踢到桌下的规定，既保护小腿，也帮了清洁人员。
collocations: kick off｜开球；开始
tip_zh: kick off 可表示比赛开球，也可比喻活动开始。

definition_en: a piece of music with words
example1_en: We learned a new song in music class.
example1_zh: 音乐课上我们学了一首新歌。
example2_en: A local song can keep a dialect alive when children no longer hear it at home.
example2_zh: 当孩子在家里不再听到一种方言时，一首本地歌曲能让它继续活着。
collocations: pop song｜流行歌曲 ; sing a song｜唱歌
tip_zh: song 是可数名词。

definition_en: a large wild cat
example1_en: The lion is in the nature book.
example2_en: A lesson about the lion should say where it can live, not how to harm it.
example2_zh: 关于狮子的课应当说它能住在哪里，而不是如何伤害它。
collocations: a lion of｜一头狮子
tip_zh: lion 可数。

definition_en: a section of a school, shop, or government
example1_en: She works in the English department.
example2_en: A health department that shares data with schools can warn them before a heatwave arrives.
example2_zh: 与学校共享数据的卫生部门，可以在热浪到来前发出警告。
collocations: department store｜百货商店
tip_zh: department 是组织里的部门或大学的系。

definition_en: the point where two lines or streets meet
example1_en: The bookshop is on the corner.
example2_en: A dark corner near the station feels unsafe even when the crime rate is low.
example2_zh: 车站附近阴暗的角落即使犯罪率很低，也会让人觉得不安全。
collocations: in the corner｜在角落里 ; around the corner｜在附近；即将来临
tip_zh: 房间角落用 in the corner。街道拐角用 on the corner。

meanings_zh: n. 锻炼；练习 | v. 锻炼
definition_en: physical activity, or a piece of work to practise | to do physical activity
example1_en: Morning exercise is in the yard.
example2_en: An exercise book full of copies is not the same as one hard problem done slowly.
example2_zh: 一本抄满的练习册，不等于慢慢做完的一道难题。
collocations: take exercise｜锻炼 ; do an exercise｜做一道练习
tip_zh: exercise 作“锻炼”时常不可数；作“习题”时可数。也可作动词。

definition_en: not hard, or not loud or bright
example1_en: The ground is soft after the rain.
example2_en: Soft light in a hallway can save energy and still show the step.
example2_zh: 走廊里柔和的灯可以省电，同时仍然照得见台阶。
collocations: soft drink｜软饮料 ; soft voice｜轻柔的声音
tip_zh: soft drink 是不含酒精的饮料。表里没有单独的 soft 音标行，本库用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: an upright side of a room or a barrier
example1_en: The notice is on the wall.
example2_en: A high wall around a school can keep children safe and also hide the street they need to learn.
example2_zh: 学校周围的高墙可以保护孩子，也会挡住他们需要认识的街道。
collocations: on the wall｜在墙上 ; wall of｜一堵……的墙
tip_zh: 在墙上用 on the wall。

definition_en: normal, not special
example1_en: It was an ordinary Monday.
example2_en: Ordinary help, such as holding a door, matters as much as a speech.
example2_zh: 扶门这样的普通帮助，和一篇讲话一样重要。
collocations: ordinary people｜普通人
tip_zh: extraordinary 是本批的另一词。

definition_en: working by itself
example1_en: The door is automatic.
example2_en: An automatic reply is not a person who can change the bus time.
example2_zh: 自动回复不是一个能改公交时间的人。
collocations: automatic door｜自动门
tip_zh: automatic 也可作名词，较少用。

definition_en: a weapon that shoots
example1_en: The museum does not allow a gun in the building.
example1_zh: 博物馆不允许把枪带进楼里。
example2_en: A history lesson about a gun should also ask who was harmed, not only how the machine worked.
example2_zh: 关于枪的历史课也应该问谁受到了伤害，而不只是机器如何工作。
collocations: gun control｜枪支管制
tip_zh: gun 是可数名词。

meanings_zh: v. 在意；关心 | n. 小心；照料
definition_en: to feel that something is important | attention or looking after someone
example1_en: She cares about every student in the class.
example1_zh: 她关心班上的每一个学生。
example2_en: People care more about a park when they helped plant the trees than when they only walk past it.
example2_zh: 人们如果参与种过树，会比只是路过时更在意一座公园。
collocations: care about｜关心 ; care for｜照顾；喜欢 ; take care｜当心
tip_zh: care for 可以是照顾，也可以是“喜欢”，要看语境。

definition_en: imagination, or a story that is not real
example1_en: The story is a fantasy, not a plan.
example1_zh: 这个故事是幻想，不是计划。
example2_en: Fantasy can open a class, and the bus time still has to be real.
example2_zh: 幻想可以打开一节课，公交时间却必须是真的。
collocations: a fantasy about｜关于……的幻想
tip_zh: fantasy 可数也可不可数。

definition_en: of the colour of gold, or excellent
example1_en: The golden light lasted ten minutes.
example1_zh: 金色的光持续了十分钟。
example2_en: A golden chance to fix the roof comes before the rainy season, not after the first leak.
example2_zh: 修屋顶的黄金机会在雨季之前，而不是第一次漏水之后。
collocations: golden opportunity｜良机
tip_zh: golden 多形容颜色或比喻“极好”。金子本身用 gold。

definition_en: the larger part of a group
example1_en: The majority of students walk or cycle.
example1_zh: 大多数学生步行或骑车。
example2_en: A majority vote can still be unfair if the people most affected were not in the room.
example2_zh: 如果受影响最大的人不在房间里，多数票仍然可能不公平。
collocations: the majority of｜大多数
tip_zh: the majority of 加复数名词时谓语常用复数。

definition_en: one of the five parts at the end of the hand
example1_en: She pointed with one finger.
example2_en: A cut on a finger in the lab is a reason to stop and wash it.
example2_zh: 实验室里手指被划伤，是停下来清洗的理由。
collocations: finger of｜一根手指
tip_zh: finger 通常不含拇指时有人用 thumb 单指拇指。本条按一般“手指”处理。

definition_en: a way of showing ideas or feelings, or a look on the face
example1_en: Her expression showed she was tired.
example2_en: Freedom of expression at school still has a limit: no one may threaten a classmate.
example2_zh: 学校里的表达自由仍有界限：谁也不能威胁同学。
collocations: facial expression｜面部表情 ; freedom of expression｜表达自由
tip_zh: 动词 express 已在本库。expression 也可指固定说法。

meanings_zh: v. 担心 | n. 烦恼；担忧
definition_en: to feel anxious about something | a problem that makes you anxious
example1_en: Do not worry about the result tonight.
example2_en: Parents worry when the last bus is cancelled and the school has not sent a message.
example2_zh: 末班车取消而学校又没发消息时，家长会担心。
collocations: worry about｜为……担心
tip_zh: worry 后接 about。形容词 worried 形容人，worrying 形容事情。

definition_en: thin cord, or the part of an instrument you play
example1_en: The parcel is tied with string.
example2_en: A broken string on the guitar is a reason to borrow another, not to cancel the song.
example2_zh: 吉他断了一根弦，是再借一把的理由，不是取消这首歌。
collocations: a piece of string｜一根绳子
tip_zh: string 作绳子时常不可数。乐器的弦可数。

definition_en: money gained after costs
example1_en: The book fair made a small profit.
example2_en: A profit from the canteen should be explained to the students who paid for lunch.
example2_zh: 食堂的利润应当向付钱吃午饭的学生说明。
collocations: make a profit｜获利 ; profit from｜从……中获益
tip_zh: profit 作动词是获益。profit from something。

definition_en: a large boat
example1_en: The ship left the port at dawn.
example2_en: Goods on a ship still need a road at the other end if a village is to receive them.
example2_zh: 如果一个村子要收到货物，船上的货在另一头仍然需要一条路。
collocations: by ship｜乘船
tip_zh: ship 作动词是“运送”。

definition_en: a person you do not know
example1_en: A stranger asked for the library.
example1_zh: 一个陌生人问路去图书馆。
example2_en: Teach students to ask an adult, not to follow a stranger.
example2_zh: 教学生去问成年人，而不是跟着陌生人走。
collocations: a stranger to｜对……陌生的人
tip_zh: strange 已在本库。本条不写跟踪或伤害的做法。

meanings_zh: n. 手臂 | v. 武装；装备
definition_en: the part of the body between the shoulder and the hand | to provide with weapons or tools
example1_en: She carried the books in one arm.
example2_en: A chair with no arm is cheaper, and it is harder for some students to stand up from.
example2_zh: 没有扶手的椅子更便宜，有些学生也更难从上面站起来。
collocations: arm in arm｜臂挽臂
tip_zh: arm 作动词是武装。家具的扶手也叫 arm。

definition_en: a dark shape made when light is blocked
example1_en: The tree throws a shadow on the path.
example2_en: A shadow on the crossing is not a light.
example2_zh: 路口的阴影不是灯。
collocations: in the shadow of｜在……的阴影里
tip_zh: shadow 可数。

definition_en: an adult female person
example1_en: A woman from the clinic spoke to our class.
example1_zh: 诊所的一位女士给我们班讲了话。
example2_en: A woman who works a night shift still needs a safe way home when the last bus has gone.
example2_zh: 上夜班的妇女在末班车走后，仍然需要一条安全的回家路。
collocations: women's day｜妇女节
tip_zh: woman 的复数是 women，读音也变。

meanings_zh: adj. 下一个的；接下来的
definition_en: coming immediately after
example1_en: The next bus leaves in ten minutes.
example2_en: The next step after collecting data is to ask whether the sample left anyone out.
example2_zh: 收集数据之后的下一步，是追问样本是否漏掉了什么人。
collocations: next to｜在……旁边 ; next week｜下周
tip_zh: next week 前不加 the；the next week 常指过去某个时间之后的一周。

definition_en: a medicine, or an illegal substance
example1_en: The drug must stay in the school clinic.
example1_zh: 这种药必须放在校医务室。
example2_en: Health class should say clearly that a drug from a doctor is not the same thing as an illegal drug.
example2_zh: 健康课应当讲清楚：医生开的药和非法毒品不是一回事。
collocations: drug store｜药店 ; illegal drug｜毒品
tip_zh: drug 既可以是正规药物，也可以是毒品。写作时要加修饰语，避免含糊。

definition_en: the organisation that keeps public order
example1_en: The police helped the children cross the road.
example1_zh: 警察帮助孩子们过马路。
example2_en: Police cannot be the only answer to a dark street; lights and pavements matter too.
example2_zh: 警察不能是黑暗街道的唯一答案；灯和人行道也很重要。
collocations: police station｜警察局 ; police officer｜警官
tip_zh: police 是集体名词，谓语常用复数。一个警察用 a police officer。

definition_en: not old
example1_en: The young trees need water every evening.
example1_zh: 这些小树每天晚上需要浇水。
example2_en: Young workers leave a town when the only jobs are far away and poorly paid.
example2_zh: 当仅有的工作又远又报酬低时，年轻工人会离开城镇。
collocations: young people｜年轻人 ; the young｜年轻人
tip_zh: the young 表示年轻人这一类，谓语用复数。

meanings_zh: v. 数；计算 | n. 计数
definition_en: to say numbers in order, or to be important | an act of counting
example1_en: Count the chairs before the parents arrive.
example2_en: Every voice should count when a class decides how to share one practice room.
example2_zh: 班级决定如何共用一间练习室时，每个声音都应当算数。
collocations: count on｜依靠 ; count as｜算作
tip_zh: count on somebody 表示依靠某人。count 也可作名词“计数”。

definition_en: the facts of a particular time
example1_en: The situation is better than last week.
example2_en: The situation on a flooded street is not the same as the situation on a dry planning map.
example2_zh: 积水街道上的情况，和干燥的规划地图上的情况不一样。
collocations: in a situation｜处于某种情况
tip_zh: situation 是可数名词。

definition_en: a picture made by a camera
example1_en: She took a photo of the old bridge.
example2_en: A photo of a clean park can hide the street where the rubbish was taken.
example2_zh: 一张干净公园的照片，可以藏起垃圾被运去的那条街。
collocations: take a photo｜拍照
tip_zh: photo 是 photograph 的简写，复数是 photos。

definition_en: every person
example1_en: Everybody in our class joined the clean-up.
example1_zh: 我们班每个人都参加了打扫。
example2_en: Everybody needs a seat at the meeting if the decision will change their bus home.
example2_zh: 如果决定会改变他们回家的公交，每个人都需要在会上有一个座位。
collocations: everybody else｜其他所有人
tip_zh: everybody 后接单数动词。和 everyone 同义，本库两条都保留。不要写成 every body（每一具身体）。

definition_en: a person who flies an aircraft
example1_en: The pilot spoke before the plane left.
example1_zh: 飞机起飞前飞行员讲了话。
example2_en: A school visit to an airport should meet the pilot and the person who loads the bags.
example2_zh: 学校参观机场应当见到飞行员，也应当见到装行李的人。
collocations: a pilot programme｜试点计划
tip_zh: pilot 也可指试点：a pilot programme。

definition_en: to keep doing something
example1_en: Please continue reading after the break.
example2_en: If factories continue to pour waste at night, daytime clean-ups will not save the river.
example2_zh: 如果工厂继续在夜里排污，白天的清理也救不了这条河。
collocations: continue to do｜继续做 ; continue doing｜继续做
tip_zh: continue 后接 to do 或 doing 都可以。

meanings_zh: n. 橙子；橙汁 | adj. 橙色的
definition_en: a round citrus fruit, or its juice | of a colour between red and yellow
example1_en: She ate an orange at the break.
example2_en: Orange juice that is mostly sugar should say so on the label.
example2_zh: 主要是糖的橙汁应当在标签上写明。
collocations: orange juice｜橙汁
tip_zh: orange 作水果可数，作颜色或果汁时常不可数。形容词是橙色的。

meanings_zh: n. 比赛；火柴 | v. 匹配；比得上
definition_en: a sports game, or a small stick for making fire | to fit or be equal to
example1_en: The football match is on Saturday.
example2_en: A cup match brings visitors, but the town still needs bins and buses after the final whistle.
example2_zh: 杯赛带来观众，但终场哨响后城镇仍需要垃圾桶和公交。
collocations: match point｜赛点 ; a box of matches｜一盒火柴
tip_zh: match 作动词是“匹配”。win a match，不说 win sb。

definition_en: the basic law of a country, or the body's condition
example1_en: The class read one article of the constitution.
example2_en: A strong constitution in a child still needs sleep, not only sport.
example2_zh: 孩子体质好，仍然需要睡眠，而不只是运动。
collocations: the constitution of｜……的宪法
tip_zh: constitution 可指宪法，也可指体质或章程。不要和 constituent 混淆。

definition_en: the organ that pumps blood, or the centre
example1_en: Regular walks are good for the heart.
example1_zh: 经常走路对心脏有好处。
example2_en: A market in the heart of a town keeps daily life there; a mall on the edge can empty the centre.
example2_zh: 镇中心的市场维持着那里的日常生活；边缘的商场可能掏空中心。
collocations: heart disease｜心脏病 ; learn by heart｜记住 ; lose heart｜丧失勇气
tip_zh: by heart 表示靠记忆，不是“靠心脏”。

definition_en: a vehicle or firework that is driven upward by burning fuel
example1_en: The textbook shows a rocket and a diagram.
example1_zh: 课本展示火箭和一张图。
example2_en: A lesson about a rocket should stay with the diagram, not a method.
example2_zh: 关于火箭的课应当停在图上，而不是做法。
collocations: a space rocket｜太空火箭
tip_zh: 本条是科普词汇。不写如何制造或发射。

meanings_zh: adj. 干的；干燥的 | v. 使变干
definition_en: not wet | to make or become dry
example1_en: Hang the coats where they can dry.
example1_zh: 把外套挂在能晾干的地方。
example2_en: A dry year raises the price of vegetables before it empties the school taps.
example2_zh: 干旱的一年会先抬高菜价，然后才会让学校的水龙头没水。
collocations: dry up｜干涸 ; dry season｜旱季
tip_zh: dry 作动词是使变干。

definition_en: written works, especially those valued as art
example1_en: We read literature from more than one country.
example1_zh: 我们读的文学不止来自一个国家。
example2_en: Literature class is richer when the list includes writers the textbook forgot.
example2_zh: 如果书单包括课本忘掉的作家，文学课会更丰富。
collocations: English literature｜英国文学
tip_zh: literature 通常不可数。

definition_en: words changed from one language into another
example1_en: The translation is on the right.
example2_en: A translation of the bus notice helps the parent who does not read the first language.
example2_zh: 公交通知的翻译能帮助读不懂第一种语言的家长。
collocations: a translation of｜……的译文
tip_zh: translation 可数。

definition_en: wanting food
example1_en: The class was hungry before lunch.
example2_en: A hungry student cannot use a speech about diet as a meal.
example2_zh: 饥饿的学生不能把一篇关于饮食的讲话当成一餐。
collocations: be hungry for｜渴望
tip_zh: hungry 是形容词。名词是 hunger。

definition_en: the state of continuing to live
example1_en: Survival after the flood depended on a dry room.
example1_zh: 洪水后的幸存靠的是一间干房间。
example2_en: The survival of a small shop depends on the rent.
example2_zh: 小店能否留下来取决于租金。
collocations: survival of｜……的幸存
tip_zh: 动词 survive 已在本库。survival 通常不可数。

definition_en: before now
example1_en: The museum closed two years ago.
example2_en: A factory that shut ten years ago can still leave chemicals in the soil beside a school.
example2_zh: 十年前关闭的工厂，仍可能把化学物质留在学校旁边的土壤里。
collocations: long ago｜很久以前 ; a moment ago｜刚才
tip_zh: ago 用于过去时，放在时间段后面：three days ago。不与现在完成时连用。

meanings_zh: adj. 成熟的 | v. 成熟
definition_en: fully grown, or behaving in a sensible adult way | to become fully grown
example1_en: The plan is mature enough to name a person.
example1_zh: 这个计划成熟到能写出一个人的名字。
example2_en: A mature reply admits a mistake.
example2_zh: 成熟的回答会承认错误。
collocations: mature enough｜足够成熟
tip_zh: mature 也可作动词“成熟”。

definition_en: the sweet part of a plant
example1_en: The canteen has fruit on Monday.
example2_en: Fruit that students can take without paying is a policy, not only a bowl.
example2_zh: 学生可以不付钱拿走的水果是一项办法，而不只是一只碗。
collocations: fruit juice｜果汁
tip_zh: fruit 作总称通常不可数。a fruit 可指一种水果。

meanings_zh: adj. 圆的 | prep. 围绕 | n. 一轮
definition_en: shaped like a circle | around | one stage of an event
example1_en: They sat at a round table.
example2_en: A round of talks about the river should include the farms upstream, not only the city.
example2_zh: 关于这条河的一轮会谈应该包括上游的农场，而不只是城市。
collocations: all the year round｜一年到头 ; round trip｜往返行程
tip_zh: 英式里 round 常作介词“围绕”；美式多用 around。

definition_en: a male child
example1_en: Her son walks to school with a neighbour.
example1_zh: 她儿子和邻居一起走路上学。
example2_en: A son who leaves for the city may still send money home, but the village loses his daily help.
example2_zh: 去城市的儿子也许仍会寄钱回家，但村子失去了他日常的帮忙。
collocations: son and daughter｜子女
tip_zh: son 的复数是 sons。

meanings_zh: n. 性格；角色 | n. 角色；人物 | n. 字符；文字
definition_en: personality; a person in a story | a person represented in a story, play, or film | a written or printed symbol, such as a letter
example1_en: Honesty is part of his character.
example1_zh: 诚实是他性格的一部分。
example2_en: Preserving historic buildings helps cities retain their distinctive character while adapting to modern economic demands.
example2_zh: 保护历史建筑有助于城市在适应现代经济需求的同时，保留自身的独特风貌。
collocations: main character｜主要角色 ; strength of character｜坚强品格 ; distinctive character｜独特风貌 ; Chinese characters｜汉字
tip_zh: 作“人物、字符”可数；作整体品质常不可数。

definition_en: something that may happen or be true
example1_en: There is a possibility of rain.
example2_en: The possibility of a late bus should be written down before the trip, not during it.
example2_zh: 晚班车的可能性应当在出行前写下来，而不是在途中。
collocations: a possibility of｜……的可能
tip_zh: possible 已在本库。possibility 是名词，后接 of 或 that。

meanings_zh: det. 两者都不 | pron. 两者都不
definition_en: not one and not the other of two | not either of two
example1_en: Neither answer is fully right.
example2_en: Neither the early bus nor the late one stops at the new housing block.
example2_zh: 早班车和晚班车都不在新建的住宅区停。
collocations: neither...nor｜既不……也不 ; neither of｜两者都不
tip_zh: neither 作主语时谓语常用单数。nor 已在本库。

definition_en: a special day or period of public celebration
example1_en: The town festival is next weekend.
example1_zh: 镇上的节日在下个周末。
example2_en: A school festival should name which dates belong to which community, and not assume one calendar.
example2_zh: 学校的节日活动应当写明哪些日子属于哪个群体，而不假定只有一种日历。
collocations: Spring Festival｜春节 ; festival of｜……节
tip_zh: festival 可数。on the festival 不如 at the festival 或 during the festival 常见。

definition_en: to get something that is given or sent
example1_en: I received your message this morning.
example1_zh: 我今天早上收到了你的信息。
example2_en: Students who receive help early are less likely to hide a problem until the exam.
example2_zh: 早点得到帮助的学生，不太会把问题藏到考试。
collocations: receive a letter｜收到信
tip_zh: 拼写是 receive：c 后面是 ei。收到并不等于接受，接受用 accept。

definition_en: a supporting structure, or a set of ideas
example1_en: The framework of the essay is three points.
example1_zh: 这篇作文的框架是三个要点。
example2_en: A framework for the bus plan should include the return time.
example2_zh: 公交计划的框架应当包括返回时间。
collocations: a framework for｜……的框架
tip_zh: framework 可数。

definition_en: perhaps
example1_en: Maybe we can meet after the club.
example1_zh: 也许我们可以在社团活动后见面。
example2_en: Maybe a later school start would help, but only if buses change their times too.
example2_zh: 也许推迟上学时间会有帮助，但只有公交也改时间才行。
collocations: maybe so｜也许如此
tip_zh: maybe 是一个副词；may be 是情态动词加动词，要分开写。

meanings_zh: n. 分数；记号 | v. 做标记；打分
definition_en: a point given for work, or a sign | to write a sign, or to give a score
example1_en: She got a high mark in the reading test.
example2_en: A single mark on one test should not decide whether a student can join the science club.
example2_zh: 一次测验的一个分数，不该决定学生能否参加科学社团。
collocations: full marks｜满分 ; mark on｜在……上的记号
tip_zh: mark 作动词是“做标记”或“打分”。

meanings_zh: n. 价值 | v. 重视
definition_en: the worth or importance of something | to think something is important
example1_en: The old map still has value for the history class.
example1_zh: 这张旧地图对历史课仍有价值。
example2_en: The value of a library is not only the books, but the quiet hour it gives after school.
example2_zh: 图书馆的价值不只是书，还有它在放学后提供的安静一小时。
collocations: of value｜有价值的 ; value of｜……的价值
tip_zh: value 作动词是“重视”或“估价”。

meanings_zh: n. 穆斯林 | adj. 穆斯林的
definition_en: a person who follows Islam | of Muslims or Islam
example1_en: The museum explains how local Muslims mark the festival.
example1_zh: 博物馆讲解当地穆斯林如何过这个节日。
example2_en: A school calendar that names one holiday should also leave room for a Muslim student to be absent for another.
example2_zh: 只写一个节日的校历，也应当给穆斯林学生为另一个节日请假留出空间。
collocations: Muslim community｜穆斯林社区
tip_zh: Muslim 作名词和形容词都要大写。表里没有这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: a formal talk, or the power of speaking
example1_en: Her speech at the ceremony was three minutes.
example1_zh: 她在典礼上的演讲只有三分钟。
example2_en: A speech that names no fact can still sound confident, which is why the class checks sources.
example2_zh: 一篇不提事实的演讲仍可能听起来自信，所以班级要核来源。
collocations: make a speech｜发表演讲 ; freedom of speech｜言论自由
tip_zh: speech 表示一次演讲时可数。表示说话能力时不可数。

definition_en: the design of buildings
example1_en: The architecture of the hall is simple.
example2_en: Good architecture includes a door a wheelchair can use.
example2_zh: 好的建筑包括一扇轮椅能用的门。
collocations: modern architecture｜现代建筑
tip_zh: architecture 通常不可数。

meanings_zh: n. 厨师 | v. 烹调；做饭
definition_en: a person who cooks | to prepare food by heating it
example1_en: The cook knows which students cannot eat nuts.
example1_zh: 厨师知道哪些学生不能吃坚果。
example2_en: A school cook who labels the food saves more trouble than a long speech about diet.
example2_zh: 给食物贴标签的学校厨师，比一篇关于饮食的长讲话更能省麻烦。
collocations: cook a meal｜做饭
tip_zh: cook 是人。炉具是 cooker。作动词是烹调。

definition_en: a large area of water surrounded by land
example1_en: We are not allowed to swim in the lake.
example2_en: A clean lake supports birds and a town's drinking water at the same time.
example2_zh: 干净的湖同时养活鸟类和一座城镇的饮用水。
collocations: by the lake｜在湖边
tip_zh: lake 是被陆地包围的湖。sea 是海。

meanings_zh: v. 表达 | n. 快车；快递 | adj. 特快的
definition_en: to show a feeling or idea in words | a fast train or delivery | travelling or sent very fast
example1_en: She could not express the idea in one sentence.
example1_zh: 她没法用一句话表达这个想法。
example2_en: Students who express a worry early give the school time to change the plan.
example2_zh: 早点说出担心的学生，给学校留下改变计划的时间。
collocations: express oneself｜表达自己 ; express train｜快车
tip_zh: express 作名词或形容词可指快车或特快。

meanings_zh: n. 标准 | adj. 标准的
definition_en: a level used for judging | usual or accepted
example1_en: The school raised its safety standard.
example2_en: A national standard for school buses helps only if villages can afford to meet it.
example2_zh: 校车的国家标准只有在乡村负担得起时才有帮助。
collocations: standard of living｜生活水平 ; up to standard｜达到标准
tip_zh: standard 作形容词是“标准的”。

definition_en: to or at a distance
example1_en: She put the phone away during dinner.
example1_zh: 晚饭时她把手机收起来了。
example2_en: Moving factories away from rivers can protect drinking water for the towns downstream.
example2_zh: 把工厂迁离河流，可以保护下游城镇的饮用水。
collocations: far away｜遥远 ; right away｜立刻 ; give away｜赠送；泄露
tip_zh: away 是副词，不单独接宾语；表示离开某地用 away from。

definition_en: inside a limit of time, distance, or area
example1_en: Please reply within three days.
example2_en: A clinic within walking distance saves families the cost of a long bus ride.
example2_zh: 步行能到的诊所，能为家庭省下长途公交的费用。
collocations: within reach｜在够得着的范围内
tip_zh: within 强调不超过某个范围；in 更一般。

meanings_zh: n. 实验 | v. 做实验
definition_en: a test done to learn something | to do a test
example1_en: The experiment is on the board.
example2_en: An experiment without notes cannot be repeated by the next class.
example2_zh: 没有笔记的实验，下一班无法重复。
collocations: do an experiment｜做实验 ; experiment with｜用……做实验
tip_zh: experiment 作动词是做实验。本条不写危险操作。

definition_en: the front of the chest, or a part of the body
example1_en: The clinic form uses the word breast in a medical sense.
example1_zh: 诊所表格在医学意义上使用 breast 这个词。
example2_en: A health lesson can name the breast and still stay respectful.
example2_zh: 健康课可以提到胸部，同时仍然保持尊重。
collocations: breast of｜……的胸部
tip_zh: breast 是身体部位的普通词。本条用医务和课堂的说法，不写其他内容。

meanings_zh: v. 触摸；接触 | n. 接触；触觉
definition_en: to put a hand on something | an act of touching, or the sense
example1_en: Do not touch the wet paint on the door.
example1_zh: 别碰门上还没干的油漆。
example2_en: A museum that lets students touch a copy of an old tool teaches more than a glass case alone.
example2_zh: 让学生触摸一件古工具复制品的博物馆，比只有玻璃柜教得更多。
collocations: keep in touch｜保持联系 ; touch on｜提及
tip_zh: keep in touch 表示保持联系，不是身体接触。

definition_en: to ask someone to come or to do something
example1_en: Invite the new student to the table.
example1_zh: 邀请新同学到这张桌子来。
example2_en: A school should invite the parent who works nights, and then choose a time they can come.
example2_zh: 学校应当邀请上夜班的家长，然后选一个他们能来的时间。
collocations: invite sb to｜邀请某人去
tip_zh: 名词常用 invitation。本库目前是动词 invite。

meanings_zh: adj. 平等的；相等的 | v. 等于
definition_en: the same in size, value, or rights | to be the same as
example1_en: The two teams had an equal chance.
example2_en: Equal time at the microphone matters when one class is louder than the other.
example2_zh: 当一个班比另一个班更吵时，话筒前相等的时间就很重要。
collocations: be equal to｜等于；胜任 ; equal rights｜平等权利
tip_zh: equal 作动词是等于。be equal to 还可表示胜任。

definition_en: to leave a place or stop doing something
example1_en: He did not quit the team; he was ill.
example1_zh: 他没有退出队伍，他是病了。
example2_en: Students who quit a subject in silence give the school no chance to help.
example2_zh: 默默放弃一门课的学生，没给学校留下帮忙的机会。
collocations: quit doing｜停止做
tip_zh: quit 后接 doing，不接 to do。过去式仍是 quit。

definition_en: to encourage something, or to care for a child in your home
example1_en: The club fosters a reading habit.
example1_zh: 社团培养学生的阅读习惯。
example2_en: Foster care should name the adult who meets the child.
example2_zh: 寄养应当写明来接孩子的成年人。
collocations: foster a habit｜培养习惯 ; foster care｜寄养
tip_zh: 表里没有这一条，本库用 espeak-ng。

definition_en: including many different kinds
example1_en: The class is diverse.
example2_en: A diverse reading list still needs books the library actually has.
example2_zh: 多样的书单仍然需要图书馆真的有的书。
collocations: diverse backgrounds｜不同的背景
tip_zh: diverse 是形容词。表里标成动词，本库按形容词写。

definition_en: the writer of a book or article
example1_en: The author of the article is a local teacher.
example1_zh: 这篇文章的作者是一位本地老师。
example2_en: An author who hides their name makes it harder to judge the facts.
example2_zh: 隐瞒姓名的作者让人更难判断事实。
collocations: author of｜……的作者
tip_zh: author 是可数名词。

definition_en: a country, or a people
example1_en: The nation celebrates this day in October.
example1_zh: 这个国家在十月庆祝这一天。
example2_en: A nation that funds rural schools changes who gets to sit a university exam.
example2_zh: 资助乡村学校的国家，会改变谁有机会参加大学考试。
collocations: the whole nation｜全国 ; nation-wide｜全国范围的
tip_zh: nation 强调人民或政治共同体。country 更常指国土。

definition_en: to act or play for an audience, or to do a duty
example1_en: The choir will perform on Friday.
example2_en: Schools perform better when the first bus arrives before the bell.
example2_zh: 如果第一班车在铃响前到达，学校会运转得更好。
collocations: perform a task｜完成任务 ; perform on stage｜登台表演
tip_zh: 名词 performance 已在本库，可指演出，也可指表现。

definition_en: a device for speaking to someone at a distance
example1_en: I left my phone in the classroom.
example2_en: A phone warning about a storm helps only the people who still have power and a signal.
example2_zh: 关于风暴的手机警报，只帮助那些还有电和信号的人。
collocations: on the phone｜在打电话 ; phone number｜电话号码
tip_zh: phone 作动词是“打电话”：phone sb。

definition_en: the quality of being important
example1_en: The importance of sleep is in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 睡眠的重要性在第一章。
example2_en: The importance of the last bus is clear on the day it does not come.
example2_zh: 末班车没来的那天，它的重要性就很清楚。
collocations: the importance of｜……的重要性
tip_zh: important 已在本库。be of importance 等于 be important，更正式。

definition_en: to fail to catch, or to feel sad someone is away
example1_en: I missed the early bus this morning.
example1_zh: 今天早上我错过了早班车。
example2_en: Students miss more than a lesson when a flood closes the only road to school.
example2_zh: 当洪水封了唯一的上学路，学生错过的不只是一节课。
collocations: miss doing｜错过做 ; miss sb｜想念某人
tip_zh: Miss 大写是对未婚女性的称呼，和动词 miss 不同。

definition_en: to send something through the air with the hand
example1_en: Do not throw bags on the stairs.
example2_en: Players who throw the ball too hard in a small hall break both windows and the game.
example2_zh: 在小礼堂里扔球太用力的人，既会打碎窗户，也会毁掉比赛。
collocations: throw away｜扔掉
tip_zh: throw 的过去式是 threw，过去分词是 thrown。

meanings_zh: v. 旅行；行进 | n. 旅行
definition_en: to go from one place to another | the activity of travelling
example1_en: We travel to school by bus.
example2_en: Waste can travel downstream farther than the factory that produced it.
example2_zh: 废物可以向下游流到比产生它的工厂更远的地方。
collocations: travel to｜去……旅行 ; travel by｜乘……旅行
tip_zh: travel 作名词“旅行”通常不可数。

definition_en: to come after, or to obey
example1_en: Follow the signs to the hall.
example2_en: Students follow a timetable, but the buses they need may follow a different one.
example2_zh: 学生遵守课表，但他们需要的公交可能遵守另一份时刻表。
collocations: follow sb｜跟随 ; as follows｜如下
tip_zh: follow 是及物动词，后面直接接宾语，通常不加 to。

definition_en: to make something clear
example1_en: Can you explain this sentence in English?
example1_zh: 你能用英语解释这个句子吗？
example2_en: Charts that explain a water shortage help a town argue for repairs before the next dry summer.
example2_zh: 解释缺水的图表，能帮助一座城镇在下一个干旱的夏天之前争取维修。
collocations: explain sth to sb｜向某人解释
tip_zh: 说 explain something to somebody，不说 explain somebody something。

definition_en: uncomfortable, or difficult to use
example1_en: The silence was awkward.
example2_en: An awkward door for a wheelchair is a design problem, not a student problem.
example2_zh: 轮椅不好用的门是设计问题，不是学生的问题。
collocations: an awkward silence｜令人尴尬的沉默
tip_zh: awkward 可形容场面、人或物体。

definition_en: a room in a hospital for patients
example1_en: The ward is quiet after nine.
example2_en: A children ward needs a chair for the parent who stays.
example2_zh: 儿童病房需要给留下来的家长一把椅子。
collocations: a hospital ward｜病房
tip_zh: ward 也可指受监护的人。本条以病房为主。

definition_en: to show
example1_en: The chart indicates the bus times.
example2_en: A sign should indicate the clinic, not only the hall.
example2_zh: 牌子应当标出医务室，而不只是礼堂。
collocations: indicate that｜表明
tip_zh: indicate 比 show 正式。

definition_en: a shiny grey-white metal
example1_en: The medal is silver, not gold.
example1_zh: 这块奖牌是银的，不是金的。
example2_en: A silver cup in a cabinet teaches less than the practice that won it.
example2_zh: 柜子里的银杯，比赢得它的那次练习教得少。
collocations: silver medal｜银牌
tip_zh: silver 也可作形容词“银色的”。

definition_en: how deep something is
example1_en: The depth of the pool is marked on the wall.
example2_en: The depth of a flood matters more than a photo of the street.
example2_zh: 洪水的深度比一张街道照片更重要。
collocations: in depth｜深入地 ; the depth of｜……的深度
tip_zh: 形容词 deep 已在本库。depth 是名词。

meanings_zh: n. 一份；副本 | v. 抄写；复制
definition_en: one of a number of the same thing | to write or reproduce the same thing
example1_en: I need a copy of the reading list.
example2_en: A library with one copy of a set text cannot serve a whole grade on the same afternoon.
example2_zh: 一套课文只有一本的图书馆，没法在同一个下午服务整个年级。
collocations: a copy of｜一份 ; copy down｜抄下
tip_zh: copy 作动词是抄写或复制。考试里照抄别人的答案是作弊。

meanings_zh: n. 数字；人物 | n. 人物；人影；身形 | v. 认为；估计
definition_en: a number; an important person | a person, their outline, or the shape of their body | to think or decide something after considering it
example1_en: The figure on the board is wrong.
example2_en: Recent employment figures suggest that investment in public transport can create substantial opportunities for local workers.
example2_zh: 近期就业数据显示，投资公共交通能为当地劳动者创造大量机会。
collocations: sales figures｜销售数据 ; a leading figure｜领军人物 ; figure out｜弄清楚 ; a rough figure｜大致数值
tip_zh: 数据常用复数figures；figure out意为弄懂。

definition_en: a very hard precious stone, or a card suit
example1_en: The museum shows a diamond, and also the tools that cut stone.
example1_zh: 博物馆展示一颗钻石，也展示切石头的工具。
example2_en: A diamond on a poster does not pay the canteen staff.
example2_zh: 海报上的钻石付不了食堂职工的工资。
collocations: a diamond ring｜钻石戒指
tip_zh: 纸牌里的方块也叫 diamond。

meanings_zh: adj. 商业的 | n. 商业广告
definition_en: related to business and profit | an advertisement on television
example1_en: The commercial street is busy on Sundays.
example2_en: Commercial pressure can make a news site publish before the facts are checked.
example2_zh: 商业压力会让新闻网站在事实核对之前就发表。
collocations: commercial centre｜商业中心
tip_zh: commercial 是形容词；commerce 是名词“商业”。

definition_en: a person with authority in an organisation
example1_en: A police officer helped the children cross.
example1_zh: 一位警官帮助孩子们过马路。
example2_en: An officer who explains a rule in plain words is more useful than a sign nobody reads.
example2_zh: 用浅显的话解释规则的官员，比没人读的牌子更有用。
collocations: police officer｜警官 ; army officer｜军官
tip_zh: officer 是人；office 是办公室。

definition_en: a strong metal made from iron
example1_en: The bridge is made of steel.
example2_en: Steel gates last, and they still need a person who will open them for a late bus.
example2_zh: 钢门耐用，但晚到的校车仍然需要有人开门。
collocations: steel industry｜钢铁工业
tip_zh: steel 作材料不可数。不要和 steal（偷）混淆。

definition_en: the male ruler of an empire
example1_en: The history text names the emperor and the year.
example1_zh: 历史课文写出皇帝和年份。
example2_en: A chapter about an emperor should also say who did the work.
example2_zh: 关于皇帝的一章也应当说是谁在干活。
collocations: an emperor of｜……的皇帝
tip_zh: emperor 可数。

definition_en: to succeed in doing something
example1_en: He worked hard to achieve his goals.
example1_zh: 他努力工作以实现目标。
example2_en: Governments can achieve significant reductions in air pollution by investing in clean energy and improving public transport.
example2_zh: 政府可以通过投资清洁能源和改善公共交通，大幅减少空气污染。
collocations: achieve success｜取得成功 ; achieve a goal｜实现目标 ; achieve a balance｜达到平衡 ; achieve results｜取得成果
tip_zh: 直接接目标或成果，不说achieve to do。

definition_en: the condition of the air at a particular time
example1_en: The weather turned cold after lunch.
example2_en: Bad weather is a poor excuse for cancelling sport if the hall is empty and safe.
example2_zh: 如果礼堂空着而且安全，坏天气就不是取消体育课的好理由。
collocations: weather forecast｜天气预报 ; in all weathers｜无论什么天气
tip_zh: weather 不可数，不说 a weather。表里这一行的音标是 wear，本库不用。

definition_en: the act of making something longer or larger
example1_en: The library got an extension until six.
example2_en: An extension of the bus route helps the students who live past the old stop.
example2_zh: 公交线路的延长能帮助住在旧站以外的学生。
collocations: an extension of｜……的延长
tip_zh: extension 可数。电话分机也叫 extension。

definition_en: the time of being young, or young people
example1_en: The club is open to local youth.
example1_zh: 这个社团对本地青年开放。
example2_en: A youth centre with no evening bus is a building many of its users cannot reach.
example2_zh: 没有夜班车的青年中心，是一座许多使用者到不了的楼。
collocations: in one youth｜在某人青年时代 ; youth club｜青年俱乐部
tip_zh: the youth 可指青年群体，谓语常用复数。

definition_en: two times
example1_en: I have read the notice twice.
example2_en: Checking a source twice is cheaper than correcting a story the whole school has already shared.
example2_zh: 把来源核对两遍，比纠正全校已经转发的故事代价更小。
collocations: twice a week｜每周两次 ; twice as big｜两倍大
tip_zh: 次数用 once、twice，三次起用 three times。

meanings_zh: n. 习俗；习惯 | adj. 定制的 | n. 惠顾；光顾
definition_en: a usual practice | made to meet a particular customer's needs | the business customers give to a shop or company
example1_en: Shaking hands is a common custom.
example2_en: Schools can introduce children to local customs while encouraging respect for traditions from other cultures.
example2_zh: 学校可以向孩子们介绍当地风俗，同时鼓励他们尊重其他文化的传统。
collocations: local customs｜当地风俗 ; an ancient custom｜古老的习俗 ; custom furniture｜定制家具 ; regular custom｜经常光顾
tip_zh: custom指风俗或惯例；customs还可指海关。

definition_en: to make music with the voice
example1_en: The class will sing after the speech.
example2_en: A hall where students can sing still needs a quiet room for those who cannot.
example2_zh: 学生能唱歌的礼堂，仍然需要一间给不能唱的人的安静房间。
collocations: sing a song｜唱歌
tip_zh: sing 的过去式是 sang，过去分词是 sung。

definition_en: to become or make larger
example1_en: The number of bikes increased this term.
example1_zh: 这学期自行车的数量增加了。
example2_en: If rents increase faster than wages, workers move farther from the jobs a city needs.
example2_zh: 如果房租涨得比工资快，工人会搬得离城市需要的工作更远。
collocations: increase by｜增加了 ; increase to｜增加到
